purpose: Hybrid native-bound use of a runspace-created type after an authored literal Add-Type guard

qualification.guard: A static member receiver follows an earlier direct function statement that tests the exact unqualified type name with -as [type] and conditionally invokes literal Add-Type -TypeDefinition.
qualification.emission: The complete function emits as a Hybrid native-bound method; Add-Type, PowerShell type lookup and QueryDosDevice stay with the PowerShell host.

validation.guardedAdmissionTests: 2/2 pass; later exact static type receiver admitted, use before guard, wrong name, wrong Add-Type parameter, assembly-qualified name, bare type value and Strict rejected
validation.independentReview: One read-only review; initial assembly-identity mechanism was not reproduced because TypeName.FullName includes the assembly name. The policy now explicitly rejects assembly-qualified names; targeted confirmation found no remaining actionable issue.

limits: Only the PSSharedGoods packet was refreshed for this compiler change; the four other pinned packets and the full net472 portfolio were not rescanned.
The real case queries the local system-drive mapping; remote rows use an in-memory provider and no remote CIM request is made.
The authored C# P/Invoke declaration and Add-Type command execute in PowerShell; this is not runtime-free type, ABI or dependency closure.
Builds used unreviewed dependency resolution and do not qualify package distribution or other platforms.
SMB cross-file type creation, arbitrary Add-Type source, bare type values, assembly-qualified names and native deployment remain outside the rule.
